title: Kali365 PhaaS -- OAuth Device Code Phishing T1528 (FBI 1-052126-PSA)
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from FBI IC3 PSA)
description:
Campaign-bound sigma detection for the Kali365 Phishing-as-a-Service kit (FBI IC3 PSA 1-052126-PSA, 21 May 2026; first observed April 2026 via Telegram-distributed kits). Detects OAuth device-code flow authentication grants on Microsoft 365 / Azure AD that may indicate device-code phishing attacks. Kali365 attack chain:
(1) Lure phishing email impersonates productivity service + delivers an active device code (~15-min validity window). (2) Victim navigates to legitimate microsoft.com/devicelogin page and pastes the code, unknowingly authorizing the attacker's session. (3) Attacker captures OAuth access + refresh tokens via attacker-controlled device polling Microsoft endpoints. (4) Persistent access to Outlook + Teams + OneDrive without password and without MFA re-challenge (T1078 Valid Accounts; tokens valid for extended period).
Detection logic flags successful Azure AD sign-in events using deviceCode flow in scope where the flow is not commonly used by the tenant. Per FBI mitigation guidance, organizations should consider Conditional Access policies that block or restrict the device-code authentication flow for non-required application classes. Tune the filter_known_legitimate_device_code_apps list per tenant (kiosks, IoT, dev tooling such as PowerShell / VS Code device-code login).
Source: Tier 1 government PSA (FBI IC3 direct; via @DarkWebInformer Twitter aggregator 2026-05-22 14.6K view amplification). Aggregated from 1 first-party source disclosure 2026-05-21.
